headline: 4/6 multisig owns RolesAuthority controlling weETHs BoringVault (T1 actions, 0-delay fast path)

findings.text: weETHs BoringVault (0x917cee801a67f933f2e6b33fc0cd1ed2d5909d88) owner()=0x000...0000 (renounced/zero). authority()=0x402DFF43b4f24b006BBD6520a11C169f81085039 (RolesAuthority). https://defipunkd.com/api/contract/read?chainId=1&address=0x917cee801a67f933f2e6b33fc0cd1ed2d5909d88&method=owner and &method=authority (block ~25101271).

RolesAuthority (0x402DFF...) owner()=0xCEA8039076E35a825854c5C2f85659430b06ec96 (4/6 Gnosis Safe). https://defipunkd.com/api/contract/read?chainId=1&address=0x402DFF43b4f24b006BBD6520a11C169f81085039&method=owner and /api/safe/owners?chainId=1&address=0xCEA8039076E35a825854c5C2f85659430b06ec96 (threshold=4, 6 owners, v1.3.0, block 25101274).

BoringVault is minimal (~100 LOC), not standard proxy (no implementation()/admin() surfaced). Control delegated to external modules (Teller, Manager, Accountant) via RolesAuthority capabilities and manage() on vault. https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x917cee801a67f933f2e6b33fc0cd1ed2d5909d88 and GitHub Veda-Labs/boring-vault.

No timelock evidenced on fast path. Execution: 4/6 multisig (via RolesAuthority role capabilities) → setAuthority/manage/set params on vault/Teller/Manager or update Merkle whitelist. Delay sum on uncontested path = 0s. Docs mention role-based/timelock in some deployments but none read on-chain for this weETHs instance.

Primary multisig: 0xCEA8039076E35a825854c5C2f85659430b06ec96 (4/6, owners surfaced, threshold 4). Controls RolesAuthority (thus vault roles, manage(), pause on Teller). Fails Security Council criteria (<7 signers). BeforeTransferHook/Teller (0x99dE9e5a3eC2750a6983C8732E6e795A35e7B861) also under same authority. https://defipunkd.com/api/safe/owners and architecture docs.

Highest tier on fast path: T1 (fund-critical). manage() on BoringVault enables arbitrary calls (potential drain/upgrade logic); RolesAuthority can set roles/params affecting withdrawals, rates, strategies. Multisig on T1 path with 0 delay and fails SC criteria. https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x917cee801a67f933f2e6b33fc0cd1ed2d5909d88 (manage functions in ABI).

steelman.red: T1 reachable with no timelock by 4/6 multisig (<7 signers, fails Security Council) via RolesAuthority → manage()/role updates on fund-holding BoringVault.
steelman.orange: T1 actions possible but through documented role-based system on audited BoringVault; multisig threshold provides some friction vs EOA/2-of-3; no evidence of unilateral EOA control or instant drain without on-chain checks.
steelman.green: Core BoringVault minimal and owner-renounced; strategies strictly Merkle-restricted; control surface is role-gated rather than broad proxy admin; many similar institutional vaults use comparable 4/6 setups without immediate loss.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because T1 reachable on 0-delay fast path by 4/6 multisig (fails Security Council criteria per rubric) via RolesAuthority owning capabilities on weETHs BoringVault; no timelock evidenced on-chain for this deployment despite mentions in broader docs. Steelman for orange stronger than red (no EOA/2-of-3) or green (no >=7d delay or SC).

headline: Exit via Teller bulkWithdraw or BoringQueue (maturity ~1h); Teller pausable by multisig with no time cap; deny lists present

findings.text: Exit functions: bulkWithdraw/bulkDeposit on TellerWithMultiAssetSupport (0x99dE9e5a3eC2750a6983C8732E6e795A35e7B861); also BoringQueue requestOnChainWithdraw + cancelOnChainWithdraw. Vault has enter/exit but primary via Teller/Queue. https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x99dE9e5a3eC2750a6983C8732E6e795A35e7B861 and docs.veda.tech.

bulkWithdraw and deposits gated by isPaused(), fromDenyList/toDenyList/operatorDenyList on Teller. Queue request is permissionless (approve + call) but fulfillment after maturity by solvers; cancel always available pre-fulfillment.

Teller has pause()/unpause()/isPaused() (currently false). Pause role held via RolesAuthority (owned by 4/6 multisig); no max duration or auto-expiry evidenced — can remain paused indefinitely until unpaused. https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x99dE9e5a3eC2750a6983C8732E6e795A35e7B861 (isPaused read).
Emergency-style pause on Teller reachable unilaterally via multisig/roles (no governance vote or time cap required). No separate governance pause distinguished.
BoringQueue: request → ~1h maturity (configurable per asset) → solver fulfillment or cancel. Queue itself not explicitly pausable in evidence but tied to overall system pause/deny.
Functions directly callable on-chain (Etherscan write or wallet). Queue fulfillment relies on third-party solvers (off-chain liveness) but request/cancel permissionless.

steelman.red: Teller pause held by 4/6 multisig with no time cap can block bulkWithdraw/exits indefinitely; deny lists add gating; queued path has external solver dependency for final claims.
steelman.orange: Core exit paths (queue request + cancel) permissionless and always available pre-fulfillment; pause is on Teller (broad but reversible); maturity short (~1h) and user can cancel; no evidence of indefinite claim-locking on finalized requests.
steelman.green: No frontend dependency for core actions; users retain cancel rights; pause not shown as infinite in practice and contracts verified/audited; short maturity + Merkle/rate safeguards limit blast.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because exit is pausable broadly by multisig (no time cap) and uses queued path with solver dependency, but request/cancel remain permissionless and maturity short; steelman for orange outweighs red (no permanent claim lock) and green (pause scope too broad for green).

headline: Depends on Accountant rate providers (off-chain), Merkle-restricted external strategies, BoringQueue solvers; mitigations (bounds, verification) limit to yield/performance impact (~unclear TVS share)

findings.text: Core external calls: ManagerWithMerkleVerification to whitelisted DeFi protocols (Aave, Morpho etc.); AccountantWithRateProviders for exchange rate (off-chain oracles/rate providers). BoringVault minimal; no direct unverified oracle calls in core. https://docs.veda.tech/architecture-and-flow-of-funds and GitHub.
Off-chain: rate providers/oracles feeding Accountant; third-party solvers for BoringQueue fulfillment. Rate providers not on-chain committee; solvers permissionless but liveness-dependent.
No material non-canonical bridge dependency for primary weETHs vault (Ethereum L1 core). Cross-chain deployments exist but not assessed as primary for this slice.
weETHs is LRT (Symbiotic/EigenLayer-linked restaking receipt). Depth 1-2; slashing/freeze risk on underlying operators but user-opted per-vault; does not cross-cut other Veda vaults.

Fallbacks: Accountant rate bounds + update frequency limits + sanity checks (LIVE); Manager Merkle verification of all strategy calls (LIVE); share lock (0 in this deployment). No evidence of second-oracle or circuit-breaker beyond bounds.
BoringQueue solvers: permissionless role; failure delays fulfillment (users can cancel and reclaim shares) — graceful degradation, not catastrophic principal loss.

Multisig via RolesAuthority can update modules (Accountant, Manager, Hook) — potential to introduce/swap rate providers or strategies, but within existing Merkle/role framework; no exit window evidenced.

steelman.red: Accountant relies on off-chain rate providers (single point of manipulation risk); solvers liveness can freeze exits; multisig can swap dependencies without long timelock; LRT underlying adds restaking risk.
steelman.orange: All strategy calls Merkle-verified and restricted; Accountant has on-chain rate/frequency bounds that catch bad reports; queue failure is cancellable (no principal loss); underlying LRT risk is user-opted and isolated per vault.
steelman.green: No unmitigated path to principal loss from external deps; Merkle + rate bounds are live and enforceable; solver dependency only delays (cancellable); core vault minimal and self-contained for custody.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because external rate providers and queue solvers can materially affect yield/performance and delay exits (Stage 1 equivalent), but live Merkle verification, rate bounds, and cancellable queue prevent principal loss. Impacted TVS unclear without exact vault TVL share but bounded by mitigations and isolation. Steelman for orange strongest.

headline: Teller has deny lists + pause for deposits/transfers; contracts support permissioned mode but core actions callable on-chain; independent paths likely exist
short_headline: Deny lists + pause gating; on-chain callable

findings.text: TellerWithMultiAssetSupport has fromDenyList/toDenyList/operatorDenyList and allowFrom/denyFrom/allowTo/denyTo/allowOperator functions. Deposits and transfers can be gated by deny lists. beforeTransfer hook enforces compliance. https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x99dE9e5a3eC2750a6983C8732E6e795A35e7B861.

No mandatory off-chain operator approval for deposit request or queue withdrawal request (permissionless). Solver fulfillment for queue is off-chain but not admission gate. Pause on Teller affects some paths.
Configurable compliance via Hook/deny lists for institutional products (address whitelisting, transfer restrictions). Frontend ToS/context not assessed as grade driver.

As DeFi primitive (BoringVault standard), direct contract calls via Etherscan/wallets/aggregators possible. Published SDKs, third-party frontends, and wallet integrations expected for such vault infra; not fully captured by official UI.
On-chain deny lists (blocklist-style) updatable via roles on Teller. Not full KYC wall but compliance tooling at contract level.
Read access permissionless (anyone can view state/balances). Write (deposit/withdraw) gated by deny lists, pause, and asset support on Teller.
ToS/compliance clauses exist for institutional focus but verbatim extraction from docs limited; deny lists provide on-chain enforcement mechanism.

steelman.red: Deny lists and pause on Teller allow privileged roles (via 4/6 multisig) to gate deposits, transfers, and some exits at contract level; permissioned withdraws in Teller variants.
steelman.orange: Core request paths (deposit/queue) permissionless unless explicitly denied; deny lists are explicit blocklist (not default-deny whitelist); independent on-chain and aggregator paths exist; operational capture low for primitive.
steelman.green: No hard contract whitelist/KYC required for all users; deny/pause are configurable tools, not blanket ban; direct on-chain access and third-party routing available; aligns with permissionless DeFi vault standard.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because contracts include deny-list gating and pause on entry/exit paths (contract-level compliance controls) while supporting permissionless requests when not denied; independent access paths exist but practical use for institutional products may route through curated interfaces. Steelman for orange best matches evidence of configurable (not absolute) gating.

headline: BoringVault + Teller verified on Etherscan; source on Veda-Labs/boring-vault GitHub; multiple audits including Certora; minimal core, no major proxy drift

Source corresponds to https://github.com/Veda-Labs/boring-vault (fork of Se7en-Seas/boring-vault) — BoringVault, ManagerWithMerkleVerification, TellerWithMultiAssetSupport match architecture. Commit not pinned but structure/files align with deployed ABIs.
Audits: multiple in boring-vault/audit folder; Certora collaboration for vault security (2026 blog). Protocol.audit_links point to Se7en-Seas audits. Covers core contracts.
Certora (formal verification) is recognized firm. Multiple audits noted on site and GitHub.
No post-audit drift evidenced in sampled sources; core minimal and stable. Modules (Teller etc.) match repo descriptions.
No proxy implementation gap; BoringVault is direct minimal contract; authority/hook are separate verified or role contracts.

steelman.red: Some peripheral modules or exact deployment commit not diffed; reliance on Etherscan ABI without full local compile match in this run.
steelman.orange: Audit scope may predate some module updates; GitHub is fork (Veda-Labs) of original; no explicit bytecode equivalence proof.
steelman.green: Main contracts verified on explorer with public matching source repo; recognized auditor (Certora) coverage; minimal immutable-style core reduces drift surface; consistent with audited BoringVault standard.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because deployed bytecode verified (Etherscan), public source repo (Veda-Labs/boring-vault) corresponds to architecture, and audits from recognized firm (Certora) cover core. No proxy implementation gap or evidenced material drift. Steelman for green strongest; unknowns are scope limits not blockers.
